recordDecisions.title: Erdős 252: irrationality of factorial divisor-sum series
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For every natural exponent k, the convergent series sum over n of sigma_k(n)/n! is irrational, unconditionally. This covers the positive-exponent Erdős 252 question and exponent zero, but not transcendence or independence of the sums.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: User-directed OpenAI Codex and Claude/Opus agents made substantive mathematical proof-construction and Lean contributions, according to PALOMAR.md; exact model versions and per-agent allocation were not preserved.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check historical priority against the problem catalogue and Pratt’s exponent-four theorem; audit convergence, coprime dilation grids, progression means and the statement-to-proof correspondence. No independent human expert review is documented. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override. The Erdős252 problem-catalogue retrieval returned HTTP403; historical priority is not independently established by that inaccessible page.
recordDecisions.comparator: The source reports a complete all-exponent settlement of the Erdős 252 target, extending previously known individual exponents. Historical priority remains source-reported.

recordDecisions.title: Aging in spherical spin-glass dynamics
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The manuscript reports results for spherical Gaussian spin-glass dynamics and its positive-semidefinite Cugliandolo–Kurchan limit: physical response, entropy/Fisher estimates, stationary translated clusters, general-spin selection and aging bounds, and stationary relaxation. The reported all-spin forward theorem covers integers p >= 3 and beta > 0; strictly positive Fisher-cost conclusions require beta > beta_d, not the boundary.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The authors’ note explicitly says the manuscript is machine-written under human supervision. GPT-6 Codex agents implemented proofs, corrected mathematical assumptions and proof routes, and reviewed formal correspondence.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check the complete-conclusions and every-raw-translated-cluster quantifiers, physical-response bridge, limit witnesses and temperature restrictions; distinguish proved aging bounds from interpretive physics claims. Only the manuscript entry point and registered scope were inspected, not every chapter. Clarify original mathematical model allocation. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: Substantial specialist spin-glass dynamics results; the inspected scope does not establish a complete resolution of every aging conjecture.

recordDecisions.title: Sharp last-iterate gradient bounds and extremal trajectories
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For smooth convex functions with L-Lipschitz gradient on real Hilbert spaces, the source reports the exact constant-step final-gradient bound L||x_0-x_*|| max{1/(1+Nh),|1-h|^N}, for all horizons N >= 0 and nonnegative steps h. It classifies sampled equality trajectories and derives sharp residual/objective-residual bounds from actual constrained proximal minimizers. Positive strong convexity, changing preconditioners and arbitrary cocoercive operators are outside scope.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: JD Jones’s Disclosure.md credits GPT-6 Astra through Codex with mathematical arguments and extensions as well as Lean formalization, under human direction.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check the uniform-divergence multiplier construction, scaling interpolation surplus, equality cases and proximal minimization bridge. Establish priority relative to Chikhi’s balancing-step certificate and Kim’s distinct normalization; do not describe the full strongly-convex conjecture as solved. No independent human specialist review is claimed. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: The source reports the full smooth-convex specialization of Taylor–Hendrickx–Glineur Conjecture 3, left open by Chikhi’s September 2026 work; separate the still-unresolved positive-strong-convexity regime.

recordDecisions.title: Hilbert functions of chopped ideals of general plane points
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The source reports the full Hilbert function of degree-d chopped ideals of general plane points over characteristic-zero fields, regular-sequence cases, least stabilization degree and its stated Expected Syzygy Conjecture consequence. No assertion for arbitrary nongeneral point configurations or positive characteristic is made.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Vlado Vojdanovski’s README and metadata explicitly acknowledge GPT-6 Codex AI-assisted Lean proof development; whether AI materially originated the informal mathematical results is not established.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Read the separately distributed manuscript’s exact general-position quantifiers and Theorem 1.1/Corollary 5.1; establish novelty and original mathematical AI role rather than inferring discovery from formalization. The primary acknowledgement is explicit but theorem-level allocation is missing. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: Source-reported specialist algebraic-geometric exact Hilbert-function and syzygy results; full global conjecture scope is not established by the inspected metadata.

recordDecisions.title: Expected syzygies imply Fröberg’s prediction through degree 2d
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Over characteristic-zero fields, assuming the source’s Expected Syzygy Conjecture, Fröberg’s predicted positively truncated Hilbert function holds through degree 2d for general degree-d forms, every positive number of variables and degree and every number of generators, on one common nonempty open set. This is a conditional implication, not an unconditional all-degree proof of Fröberg’s conjecture.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The author’s primary metadata explicitly attributes Lean proof development to coordinated GPT-6 Codex agents; the original informal proof’s AI contribution is not specified.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Read the separately distributed manuscript and reconcile the Expected Syzygy premise with the chopped-plane theorem and existing record 3976. Establish original mathematical AI allocation and novelty of this conditional implication; neither full Fröberg nor all characteristics is proved by the reported statement. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: A conditional structural implication, distinct from record 3976’s sufficiently-many-variables result; neither resolves all degrees of Fröberg’s conjecture.

recordDecisions.title: A lower bound of 21 for 3-by-3 matrix multiplication over every field
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Every exact bilinear algorithm multiplying two 3-by-3 matrices over an arbitrary field uses at least 21 products of input linear forms, with unrestricted forms and output matrices, in every characteristic and for finite or infinite fields. This is not a border-rank or unrestricted arithmetic-circuit lower bound, nor an exact rank determination.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Andrey Ivanov’s pinned README/metadata credit substantial ChatGPT/Codex mathematical exploration and proof development, not only exposition. Exact historical model identities were not recorded.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit the algebraic-closure reduction, rank-minimizing replacement and atom/conductor cases; independently establish novelty relative to field-specific bounds and any earlier general-field improvement. Check the standard-Mathlib public interface and exact formal correspondence; no independent peer review is documented. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: Reported improvement from the classical general-field lower bound 19 to 21; stronger F2 and integer-coefficient results do not imply the same bound over all fields.

recordDecisions.title: A uniform zero-free half-plane for every Dedekind zeta function
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For every number field K, the source reports no zeros of its Dedekind zeta function in Re(s) > 5999/6000, excluding the pole s=1. The formal checkpoint asserts a holomorphic continuation away from 1 agreeing with Mathlib’s zeta function in Re(s)>1. The separate Hecke L-function corollary and the full generalized Riemann hypothesis are not included.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Dean Cureton and Jesse Thorner directed mathematical research and judgments; the Axiom Math owner README states AxiomProver generated the proofs and Lean formalization.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: The versioned Hexagon manuscript retrieval returned HTTP 403; inspect Theorem 1.1 and Section 15 when accessible. Independently audit the Dedekind-zeta continuation, metaplectic/automorphic bridges, statement correspondence and reused source dependencies. Establish earliest visibility and historical priority; registry registration and source-reported builds are not independent peer review. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: A source-reported fixed zero-free half-plane for every number field crosses the classical quasi-generalized-Riemann frontier, but is much weaker than Re(s)=1/2. Classification is conditional on the exact reported theorem, not proof acceptance.

recordDecisions.title: Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital nets in every dimension
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For every s >= 3 and integer base q whose prime factors are at least s-1, explicit digital (0,sk,s)-nets with q^(sk) points have covering radius at most sqrt(s)N^(-1/s). For q >= 5a_s+4 they have toroidal and Euclidean separation at least (1-a_s/q)N^(-1/s), with the source’s explicit dimension-dependent a_s and restricted first-order sharpness. This does not assert the separation bound for every small admissible base or every arbitrary cardinality.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Leonhard Gruenschloss’s README explicitly states Claude Opus 5.5 produced the constructions, proofs and formalization under author direction, with early Claude Fable 5.1 exploration.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check admissible-base restrictions, the Babai-rounded column construction, separation/covering and first-order sharpness. Read the complete historical open-problem source and establish priority; author signoff is for the headline statement, not independent peer review of every proof. External hypotheses in ancillary library claims are not premises of the headline theorem. The Zenodo creation timestamp is Oct12 London but its metadata publication date is Oct13; retain that discrepancy. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: Source-reported resolution of the higher-dimensional quasi-uniform digital-net construction problem, with substantive base and cardinality restrictions; historical breadth and priority still need checking.

recordDecisions.title: Optimality and uniqueness of Romik’s ambidextrous sofa
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Every compact connected planar shape admitting continuous rigid motions through both left- and right-turning unit-width hallways from the same starting orientation has area at most M=1+4Y^2+arctan(Y), where 4Y^3+3Y=1 and Y>0. Equality holds exactly for rotations/translations of Romik’s sofa, whose feasible motions and area are also supplied. This is the ambidextrous problem, not a new solution of the already-solved ordinary moving-sofa problem.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The-Anh Vu-Le’s owner README and metadata say ChatGPT Pro 6 found the proof and first Lean draft; Claude Opus 5.5 compiled/repaired and simplified the formalization; GPT-6 Codex wrote the accompanying manuscript under human direction.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit same-starting-orientation semantics, arbitrary continuous motions, the two-cap upper bound, equality reconstruction and imported Baek ordinary-sofa theorem. Inspect the original research notes and exact first-public history; no person has checked the proofs. Registration and reported kernel checks are not independent human specialist review. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: The exact Romik ambidextrous optimum, proposed in 2016 and still explicitly open in the 2025 exploration-at-scale paper §6.63, is reported completely settled, including uniqueness. Historical difficulty is distinct from correctness.

recordDecisions.title: Rigidity, signed-weight and stability extensions for qubit cloning
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary archive/manuscript report or public registration; earlier repository visibility is not established.
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Beyond the classical 5/6 universal cloning and asymmetric trade-off bounds, the source reports uniqueness under the six-Pauli-state average-fidelity criterion, signed real-weight asymmetric inequalities with (2a+b)(a+2b)>=0 and equality classification, and stability: average fidelity at least 5/6-epsilon implies total squared Kraus distance to the Buzek–Hillery span at most 6epsilon and channel Frobenius distance at most 200sqrt(epsilon)||rho||_F. The result uses finite Kraus families; it does not newly discover the classical cloning bound, establish Choi–Kraus, or identify six-state averages with Bloch-sphere averages.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: JD Jones’s DISCLOSURE.md credits Claude/Claude Code with proof development, certificates and prior-art review, and a GPT pre-submission consult with proposed extensions subsequently adopted after source-reported checks.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Verify which rigidity/signed-weight/stability extensions are genuinely new beyond Keyl–Werner, Hashagen and the full-region literature; audit the finite-average criterion, signed-weight domain, equality cases and constants. Exact model versions are not fully surfaced, and no independent human review or source-author endorsement is claimed. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: Source-reported mathematical extensions and quantitative stability beyond formalization of the known optimal cloning bound; novelty of the individual extensions remains open to checking.

recordDecisions.title: The rank of 3-by-3 matrix multiplication over F2 is 23
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The paper reports exact tensor rank 23 for 3-by-3 matrix multiplication over the two-element field: Laderman’s upper bound is matched by a computer-assisted exclusion of rank-22 decompositions. It does not determine the exact rank over every field or border rank.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Tejasvi Singh Tomar’s primary paper explicitly says generative AI tools found and proved the results, wrote programs and the Lean formalization, and drafted the text; exact model versions are not surfaced in this acknowledgement.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently audit completeness of the symmetry-class enumeration and rank-22 obstruction certificates. The largest formal checks use compiled native_decide evaluation, which adds trust assumptions distinct from kernel-only proofs. Establish historical priority for the exact F2 endpoint and theorem-level human/model allocation; do not generalize the field-specific conclusion. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: An exact finite-field tensor-rank frontier previously bounded below by 22 and above by 23 is reported closed. This settles the F2 case, not the all-field Laderman optimality question.

recordDecisions.title: A lower bound of 22 for integer-coefficient 3-by-3 matrix multiplication
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The paper reports at least 22 products for integer-coefficient bilinear 3-by-3 matrix multiplication, excluding an integer-constant 3-by-3 recursive algorithm that beats Strassen. Its computational proof uses field-specific quotient bounds and certificates; it is not an all-fields rank-22 theorem or an exact rank determination.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Isaac Rudich and Louis-Martin Rousseau’s paper explicitly says human-directed Claude agents wrote search code and Lean proofs; the audit surface was human-designed.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit quotient lower bounds, certificate completeness and the human-designed audit surface, and separate computational search from formal proof checks. Establish exact model allocation and independently replay the certificates; no independent verification is asserted by this refresh. Later Tomar F2 rank-23 is a distinct stronger package, not this paper’s claimed scope. Independently audit statement-to-manuscript correspondence and exact proof/certificate receipts; source-reported machine checks are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: A material bounded improvement from 21 to 22 for integer-coefficient algorithms; it does not settle the full exact-rank question.
